docs.text:
CLI-FIRST AI RESEARCH ASSISTANT One Command. Search Anything.

Zuni brings AI-powered research to your terminal. Ask a question, get an answer, and keep your workflow where it belongs.

Get Started → View on GitHub zuni 
$ zuni ask "What is quantum computing?"

information in fundamentally different ways from
classical computers.

⌘ CLI First

Designed for developers, students, and anyone who prefers a terminal-based workflow.

◈ AI Powered

Connect Zuni to compatible AI models and turn questions into useful answers.

→ 02 Research

→ 03 Answer

docs.title: What is Zuni?
docs.text: A small CLI that sends a question to an AI model and prints the answer in your terminal.

docs.title: Is it free?
docs.text: Zuni is free and open source (MIT). Model usage depends on your provider. OpenRouter offers free models such as openrouter/free.

docs.title: Which providers work?
docs.text: Any provider with an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint: OpenRouter, OpenAI, local servers like Ollama, and more.

docs.title: Does Zuni store my questions?
docs.text: No. Zuni only saves your configuration locally. Your question is sent to the provider you configured, so their privacy policy applies.

docs.title: Where is my API key stored?
docs.text: In plain text at ~/.config/zuni/config.json. Restrict access with chmod 600.

docs.title: Can I use it offline?
docs.text: Yes, with a local model server such as Ollama. Set its URL as your base URL.

docs.title: Does it search the web?
docs.text: Not yet. Web search is on the roadmap.

docs.title: Can I have a conversation with follow-ups?
docs.text: Not yet. Each zuni ask is a separate question.

docs.title: How do I change the model?
docs.text:
zuni config

or edit ~/.config/zuni/config.json.

docs.title: How can I help?
docs.text: See Contributing.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Zuni is early and evolving. This page shows where it stands and where it is heading.

docs.text:
• zuni ask for one-command questions

  • OpenAI-compatible provider support

Note

Plans may change. Open an issue to suggest or vote on ideas.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions of all sizes are welcome: bug fixes, features, docs and ideas.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni.git
cd Zuni
uv sync
uv run zuni --help

uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository

  2. Create a branch

    git checkout -b feature/my-change

  3. Make your changes

  4. Test them locally
  5. Commit with a clear message
  6. Push and open a pull request

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Use short, descriptive messages:

feat: add streaming responses
fix: handle missing config file
docs: expand installation guide
Prefix Use for feat New features fix Bug fixes docs Documentation refactor Code cleanup with no behavior change

docs.title: Code guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep functions small and documented
  • Use type hints
  • Prefer async code for network calls
  • Follow the existing style
  • Never commit API keys or config files

docs.title: Documentation guidelines
docs.text:
• Update the docs when behavior changes
  • Add runnable examples
  • Keep pages short and scannable

docs.title: Good first contributions
docs.text:
• Better error messages for failed API calls
  • Handling a missing config file gracefully
  • Tests for config.py and llm.py
  • Improving the docs

docs.title: Reporting issues
docs.text:
Open an issue at github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni/issues and include:

  • The command you ran
  • The full output or error
  • Your OS and Python version (python --version)
  • Your Zuni version

Warning

Remove API keys from any logs before posting.

docs.title: pyproject.toml at a glance
docs.text:
[project]
name = "zuni"
requires-python = ">=3.14"

[project.scripts]
zuni = "zuni.cli:main"

[build-system]
build-backend = "uv_build"

docs.title: Adding a new command
docs.text:
1. Open src/zuni/cli.py

  2. Add a function under the main group:

    @main.command()
async def hello():
    """Say hello."""
    ac.echo("Hello from Zuni!")

  3. Run uv run zuni hello

  4. Document it in docs/guide/commands.md

docs.title: Adding a new prompt
docs.text:
1. Create src/zuni/prompts/my_prompt.md

  2. Register it in prompt.py:

    def Prompt() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {
        "system": extract_prompt("system.md"),
        "my_prompt": extract_prompt("my_prompt.md"),
    }

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Zuni works with any OpenAI-compatible API. OpenRouter is the default.

docs.title: Interactive setup
docs.text:
zuni config
Prompt What to enter Example API key Your provider key (hidden while typing) sk-or-v1-... Model ID The model you want to use openrouter/free Base URL The API root of your provider https://openrouter.ai/api/v1

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
Settings are stored here:

OS Path Linux / macOS / Termux ~/.config/zuni/config.json Windows C:\Users\<you>\.config\zuni\config.json 
{
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "MODEL": "openrouter/free",
    "BASE_URL": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
}

You can edit this file by hand at any time.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Overrides Required OPENROUTER_API_KEY API_KEY in the config file No ZUNI_BASE_URL BASE_URL in the config file No Bash / ZshFishPowerShell 
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export ZUNI_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

set -Ux OPENROUTER_API_KEY "your-api-key"
set -Ux ZUNI_BASE_URL "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY = "your-api-key"
$env:ZUNI_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

Add the export line to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to make it permanent.

docs.title: How values are resolved
docs.text:
Value 1st choice 2nd choice Fallback API key OPENROUTER_API_KEY config file error Model config file none openrouter/free Base URL ZUNI_BASE_URL config file none

Note

The config file should exist even if you use environment variables, because the model is always read from it. Run zuni config once to create it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Warning

Never commit your API key or config.json to Git. If a key leaks, revoke it from your provider dashboard immediately.

Tighten file permissions on Linux, macOS and Termux:

chmod 600 ~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: Reset
docs.text:
rm ~/.config/zuni/config.json
zuni config

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Get Zuni running in under a minute.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Version Notes Python 3.14 or newer Check with python --version uv latest Fast Python package and tool manager API key any OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible provider Internet required Zuni calls a hosted model

docs.title: 1. Install uv
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)pip 
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

pip install uv

Restart your terminal, then confirm:

uv --version

docs.title: 2. Install Zuni
docs.text:
uv tool install git+https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni

This installs zuni in its own isolated environment and puts the command on your PATH.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
zuni --help

You should see the ask and config commands listed.

docs.title: 4. Configure
docs.text:
zuni config

Continue with Configuration.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
Use this if you want to edit the code.

git clone https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni.git
cd Zuni
uv sync
uv run zuni --help

Tip

Run uv tool install --editable . inside the repo to get a global zuni command that reflects your local changes.

docs.title: Update
docs.text: uv tool upgrade zuni

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
uv tool uninstall zuni
rm -rf ~/.config/zuni   # optional: remove saved configuration

docs.title: If the command is not found
docs.text:
Make sure uv's tool directory is on your PATH:

uv tool update-shell

Then restart your terminal. More fixes are in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Zuni is a small async CLI. It sends one question to an OpenAI-compatible API and renders the reply.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
zuni ask "question"
      │
      ▼
   cli.py ──────────► prompts/  (load system prompt)
      │
      ▼
   llm/config.py     (API key, model, base URL)
      │
      ▼
   llm/llm.py ──────► POST /chat/completions
      │
      ▼
   rich renders the Markdown answer

docs.title: cli.py
docs.text:
Entry point registered as zuni in pyproject.toml.

  • Defines the main command group
  • config command: prompts for settings and saves them
  • ask command: builds the chat and prints the reply

docs.title: llm/config.py
docs.text:
Handles configuration.

Function Purpose api_key() Reads the key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then the config file model() Reads the model from the config file, defaults to openrouter/free baseUrl() Reads ZUNI_BASE_URL, then the config file load_config() Loads ~/.config/zuni/config.json save_config() Writes the config file Config() Returns all three values as a dictionary

docs.title: llm/llm.py
docs.text:
The LLM class wraps the API call.

Method Purpose headers() Builds the Authorization and Content-Type headers payload() Builds the request body (model, messages, optional tools) ask() Sends the request with httpx.AsyncClient and returns the JSON

docs.title: prompts/
docs.text: File Purpose prompt.py Reads prompt files and exposes them through Prompt() system.md System prompt that defines Zuni's behavior

docs.title: Request payload
docs.text:
{
    "model": "openrouter/free",
    "messages": [
        { "role": "system", "content": "You are Zuni..." },
        { "role": "user", "content": "Explain how DNS works" }
    ]
}

docs.title: Response handling
docs.text:
The reply is read from:

response["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

and rendered with rich.markdown.Markdown.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Package Used for asyncclick Async command-line interface httpx Async HTTP client rich Markdown rendering in the terminal

docs.title: System prompt rules
docs.text:
system.md sets these behaviors:

  • Be accurate, concise and useful
  • Never fabricate information and state uncertainty
  • Cite only sources that were provided
  • Break complex problems into steps
  • Avoid greetings and filler, optimize for the terminal
  • Decline harmful requests and offer a safe alternative

docs.title: Design choices
docs.text:
• Async first: built on asyncclick and httpx so features like streaming and parallel tool calls fit naturally
  • Provider neutral: only the standard chat completions format is used
  • Small surface: two commands, four modules

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
zuni [COMMAND] [ARGUMENTS]
Command Purpose zuni ask Ask a question and read the answer in your terminal zuni config Save API key, model and base URL zuni --help Show all commands

docs.title: zuni ask
docs.text:
Sends your question to the configured model and renders the reply as Markdown.

zuni ask "Explain how DNS works"

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
zuni ask PROMPT
Argument Required Description PROMPT Yes Your question, wrapped in quotes

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. The system prompt is loaded
  2. Your question is added as the user message
  3. The request goes to POST {BASE_URL}/chat/completions
  4. The answer is printed with formatting (headings, lists, code blocks)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
LearningCodingQuick facts 
zuni ask "What is the difference between TCP and UDP?"
zuni ask "Explain recursion like I am 12"

zuni ask "Write a Python function to reverse a string"
zuni ask "What does git rebase do?"

zuni ask "Summarize the CAP theorem in 3 lines"
zuni ask "Convert 72 F to Celsius"

docs.title: Quoting tips
docs.text:
# Good
zuni ask "What is Python's GIL?"

# Bad: the apostrophe breaks unquoted input
zuni ask What is Python's GIL?

Use single quotes if your question contains $ or !:

zuni ask 'What does $PATH do?'

docs.title: Shell tricks
docs.text:
Pipe a file into your question:

zuni ask "Explain this code: $(cat main.py)"

Save an answer to a file (formatting will be plain text):

zuni ask "List 5 Linux commands" > answer.txt

Create a short alias:

alias z='zuni ask'
z "What is a mutex?"

docs.title: zuni config
docs.text:
Interactively saves your settings.

zuni config

You are asked for the API key, model ID and base URL. The result is written to ~/.config/zuni/config.json.

See Configuration for all options.

docs.title: Help
docs.text:
zuni --help
zuni ask --help
zuni config --help

docs.title: zuni: command not found
docs.text:
uv's tool directory is not on your PATH.

uv tool update-shell

Restart the terminal and try again.

docs.title: RuntimeError: Configuration File doesn't exists!
docs.text:
Zuni could not find ~/.config/zuni/config.json.

zuni config

If zuni config itself fails with this error, create the file manually:

mkdir -p ~/.config/zuni
cat > ~/.config/zuni/config.json <<'JSON'
{
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "MODEL": "openrouter/free",
    "BASE_URL": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
}
JSON

docs.title: RuntimeError: API_KEY is not present in env or config file.
docs.text:
No key was found. Set one:

export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your-api-key"

or run zuni config.

docs.title: KeyError: 'choices'
docs.text:
The API returned an error instead of an answer. Common causes:

Cause Fix Invalid or expired API key Create a new key and run zuni config Wrong model ID Check the exact ID on your provider's model list Rate limit or no credits Wait, or switch to a free model Wrong base URL It must end at the API root, such as /v1

docs.title: Connection or timeout errors
docs.text:
• Check your internet connection
  • Confirm the base URL has no typos
  • Try again later if the provider is down

docs.title: Python version error
docs.text:
Zuni needs Python 3.14 or newer.

python --version
uv python install 3.14

docs.title: The answer looks plain or unformatted
docs.text: Formatting only appears when printing to a terminal. Redirecting output to a file (> file.txt) removes it.

docs.title: Docs page looks outdated
docs.text: Hard refresh the browser, or clear the site cache, so the latest CSS loads.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Open an issue with your command, full error and Python version: github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni/issues.
